_about: Published figures used by model/flows.py for the chapter 'flows'. 'lines': passengers a working day on a whole line, used to set the stations that have no count (RER A and B, whose RATP stations in Paris are not counted line by line; RER E, whose 2022 count is older than its extension to Nanterre). 'published': the same kind of figure for the other lines, shown beside the counts, not used in the fit. 'ter': passengers a working day on regional express trains at a Paris terminal. 'places': places on a full train of the line at the peak, seated and standing. 'capacity': trains an hour each way that a section is said to take. Each entry names its source by the key of src/sections/flows/sources.json.

A.note: up to 1.3 million a day (RATP, 2024); the Cour des comptes wrote 1.4 million in 2023

B.note: 983,000 a day in 2019; about one million in 2026

E.note: 370,000 a day when the full service to Nanterre began; 600,000 expected

B.note: derived: the future MI20 holds 1,063 a unit, said to be up to 35% more than today's; two units a train

D.note: derived: two RER NG units of 130 m hold 3,722, about 550 more than two of the older Z 2N units that still run most trains

E.note: two RER NG units of 112 m

P.note: two Francilien units of 8 cars; other trains run on some branches

BD.note: 20 RER B and 12 RER D an hour each way in the timetable; about 28 run in practice

E.note: 16 an hour at the peak today; 22 aimed at with the new signalling

LGVSE.note: 13 an hour each way at the peak today, 16 from 2030
